action_type_raw: Cancellation of service approval as an effect of the Provider cancellation (Section 34 Effect of cancellation)
reason: Provider Approval Cancelled -Section 31 of the National Law, which states that the Regulatory Authority may cancel a provider approval if: (a) the Regulatory Authority is satisfied that the approved provider or a person with management or control of an education and care service operated by the approved provider is not a fit and proper person to be involved in the provision of an education and care service; (b) the Regulatory Authority is satisfied that the continued provision of education and care services by the approved provider would constitute an unacceptable risk to the safety, health or well-being of any child or class of children being educated and cared for by an education and care service operated by the approved provider; (e) the approved provider has breached a condition of the provider approval. Section 21 of the National Law provides that the Regulatory Authority may at any time assess whether an approved provider continues to be a fit and proper person to be involved in the provision of an education and care service. Section 13 of the National Law applies to that assessment and outlines the matters to be considered in determining whether a person is a fit and proper person. The Regulatory Authority must consider the matters set out in subsections 13(1) and may consider the matters set out in subsection 13(2) when determining fitness and propriety. However, in accordance with subsection 13(3), it is not limited to those matters.
